title: Engineer-first greenpath: Hosted API pricing & quickstart messaging
body:
Summary:
This brief proposes a developer-first messaging axis for the Hosted API centered on two promises: (1) get a production-ready LLM endpoint in minutes, and (2) predictable token economics with ops-friendly controls. The copy and experiments below are designed to reduce engineer friction, elevate trust for platform teams, and create clear pricing anchors for self-serve conversions.

Target personas:
- Individual engineer / small team (prototype phase): fast time to first inference, low cognitive load, clear free-credits path.
- Product/ML engineer (ship to production): predictable latency, per-route cost visibility, version pinning.
- Platform/infra owner (enterprise purchase): SLA, private deployments, audit & KMS.

Core value props (developer-first framing):
1) Instant end-to-end: "From repo to request in under 10 minutes" — quickstart templates, language SDKs, and a starters collection (chat, summarization, embed).
2) Predictable unit economics: per-token transparency, per-route breakdowns, and a budgeting guardrail for spike protection.
3) Production hygiene by default: model pinning, canary rollouts, and sound defaults for batching and KV cache.
4) Ops observability without noise: token-level cost traces, latency heatmaps, and simple traces you can hand to SRE.
5) Portable contract: same API surface across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private so teams can start hosted and move to dedicated/private with minimal changes.

Proof points & talking bullets (short):
- "Ship a chat demo in 8 minutes with our Node SDK and starter prompt pack."
- "Reduce token spend by 15–40% using our batcher + prefix cache recommendations on typical support-chat loads."
- "Canary rollout to 5% of traffic in the Console; automatic fallback to smaller model if capacity strained."
- "Token-level cost traces map directly to routes, users, and sessions."

Competitive posture notes (quick scan):
- Against big cloud ML endpoints: emphasize lower per-token traceability, smarter batching defaults, and opinionated actions (auto-cache) that reduce engineering lift. Big clouds advertise model access; we advertise predictable output economics and ops readiness.
- Against API-focused LLM vendors: lean on production guarantees (routes + SLA + rollouts) and the portability story (start hosted → dedicated/private).
- Against self-hosted runtimes: highlight onboarding time, continuous kernel/optimization updates, and managed fallbacks—plus lower operational risk.

Quickstart angles (one-minute hooks and first-10-min flows):
- 60s elevator (for docs landing): "Sign up, paste your API key in sample app, and run: a 5-line call returns streaming chat. We show latency, cost, and a starter prompt pack — you’ll have a demo in 5 minutes."
- 5–10 minute guided path: 1) Create account and project. 2) Run CLI scaffold (node/python). 3) Paste example prompt + run sample. 4) Observe token and latency traces in Console. 5) Toggle model pin and enable canary.
- Starter repo names: repo-infer-chat-starter, repo-embed-search-starter (keep short).

Pricing language drafts (microcopy and anchors):
- Headline framing: "Usage that scales with what you build — clear unit rates and guardrails."
- Anchor tiers (self-serve): Free (starter credits) • Pay-as-you-go (per-token + embeddings unit) • Reserved (monthly committed throughput) • Enterprise (private + SLA + retention).
- Microcopy lines: "Per-token pricing listed on the dashboard; see estimated monthly spend for your routes before you deploy."
- Cost-control features to foreground: per-route caps, burst protection, suggested batching profile, and auto-eviction of stale KV cache.
- Pricing experiment suggestions: offer a low-lift trial that credits 10k tokens for 'first model' + a 'simulation mode' that shows monthly estimates for projected QPS without billing.

Suggested billing copy for the pricing page (short variants):
- Concise: "Pay for what you use — tokens for generation and units for embeddings. Start free, scale with reserved commits."
- Engineer-facing: "Per-token visibility, per-route caps, and a simulation mode so you can see costs before you ship."
- Platform lead: "Reserved capacity and SLA-backed latency targets for production traffic. Private deployments for compliance needs."

Objections & counters (sales + doc notes):
- "We need tighter cost controls than PAYG." → "Reserved capacity + per-route caps + automatic batching and cache recommendations to reduce spend."
- "We already self-host to control costs." → "Self-hosting can reduce model costs but increases ops burden; we provide migration paths and conservative cost/latency comparisons based on your workload profile."
- "How do I trust output quality?" → "Ship with model pinning and eval suites; Redwood Optimize recommendations help pick quantization profiles that maintain quality."

Quick experiments to validate messaging (A/B test ideas):
- Button CTAs: "Try a demo in 5 minutes" vs "See pricing & simulation" — measure clicks -> account creation -> first call.
- Onboarding wording: "Starter repo + 10k credits" vs "Starter repo + simulation mode" — measure percent that run sample call and link to Console.
- Pricing page anchor test: show per-token cents vs show estimated $/month for mapped workloads.

Metrics to track for success:
- Time-to-first-call (target < 10 minutes) by cohort.
- % of accounts that enable per-route caps within first 7 days.
- Conversion from PAYG -> Reserved within 60 days for accounts with >=X monthly spend.
- NPS or sentiment from Platform engineers in pilot accounts.

Open questions / decisions needed:
- Which starter repo do we bake into the signup flow (node only vs node+python)? Recommendation: ship both but default to node for the first-run experience.
- Exact free credit amount for aggressive conversion: 10k vs 25k token credit? Recommendation: 10k + simulation mode is lower-dollar but shows value.
- Pricing copy localization: when do we add region-specific pricing? Suggest delayed phase: roll it out as reserved + enterprise expand.

Appendix: example microcopies for product surfaces
- Signup CTA: "Try Redwood Hosted — demo in under 10 minutes"
- Console top banner: "Estimating costs for this route — toggle simulation to preview monthly spend."
- SDK README header: "Run the sample in 3 lines. Streaming response and cost example included."

Next steps:
- Pair with Product to create the two starter repos and one-click CLI scaffold.
- Design to produce pricing page variants for A/B tests.
- Ship a Console experiment to measure time-to-first-call and simulation usage.

Notes to reviewers (quick):
- This brief intentionally keeps developer-first language simple and metric-driven. Look for friction points in signup and first call; identify where we can instrument faster.
- If you have a competing copy variant, add it inline in the repo PR (linked above) and we’ll iterate based on initial cohort metrics.

(End)
